name: Everest Group
key_signal: EG trades at just 6.3x forward earnings and ~1.0x book value while breaking out to near 52-week highs with a golden cross and accelerating momentum (mom_126d +18.8%).
thesis: Everest Group combines rare value with strong technical momentum: trailing P/E of 7.8x and forward P/E of 6.3x are well below historical reinsurance multiples, and price-to-book near 1.0x suggests the market isn't yet crediting improved underwriting discipline. Earnings growth of 230%+ (rebound from prior cat-loss years) is driving a 'buy' consensus among all 15 covering analysts, and the stock is confirming this with price action—above both the 50- and 200-day moving averages, a golden cross intact, MACD histogram strongly positive, and 21-day momentum of 13.3%. A low beta (0.29) makes this a defensive compounder that's also re-rating higher, and the 2.09% dividend yield adds a total-return cushion while the market prices in continued hard reinsurance pricing and disciplined capital deployment (13.8% ROE, 20%+ operating margins).
bear_case: The rally has pushed RSI to 68.4 and price to within 1% of the 52-week high ($385.69), leaving little room for disappointment after a 13% one-month and 19% six-month run—any soft-market pricing commentary in reinsurance renewals (January 1 treaty season) could trigger a sharp pullback given how extended the technicals are. More fundamentally, revenue growth is already negative (-4.7%), signaling that reinsurance rates may be past peak and premium volumes are softening as capacity returns to the market post-2023/2024 hard market; the eye-popping 230% earnings growth is a low-base comparison against a bad prior year for cat losses, not a repeatable structural improvement, so multiple expansion from here is a bet on a rate cycle that consensus already believes is turning against underwriters.
